text:
sylvia: Quick RFC follow-up — planning API grace periods and compatibility adapters for upcoming /v4 endpoints. Need input on migration windows, telemetry hooks, and whether we should ship a lightweight compatibility adapter in the runtime.

raj: +1. Important to define metrics we'll use to decide when to cut the grace period. success criteria? error fallout? client adoption rate?

maria: I'd prioritize adoption rate and error budgets. If >95% calls migrate within 90 days, we can start deprecation. Also need a way for clients to opt-in to strict mode for faster failure.

tim: For runtime adapter: prefer adapter as a policy layer (proxy) that rewrites client /v3 calls to /v4 with feature flags. Keeps SDKs unchanged temporarily.

leena: How heavy is the adapter? If it becomes long-lived we end up with maintenance debt. Can we generate the adapter from the API spec? (e.g., openapi transforms)

raj: Good point. Generated adapters + opt-in telemetry would minimize manual drift. Also need to surface behavioral diffs: responses that change shape or default values.

sylvia: Proposal: 3-phase plan
1) telemetry + diff collectors (10w)
2) generated compatibility adapter in runtime (canary) + SDK hints (8w)
3) public deprecation schedule + hard cut after 180 days if adoption >95% (2w)

maria: Can we add a "compat-warning" header in responses so SDKs can log it automatically? e.g., ```X-Redwood-Compat: v3->v4-warning```

tim: yep. Also emit structured events to logs/trace with fields: client_id, route, compat_version, conversion_steps.

leena: What about function/tool calling changes? If /v4 introduces stricter typing, adapter must validate and either transform or return 400s flagged to dev team.

raj: For non-transformable changes, adapter should return a 4xx with a code that maps to upgrade guidance. That allows us to count blockers.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary: compat-adapter-staging v0.1 deployed (staging). See https://staging-console/... :rocket:

sylvia: Nice. Next: SDK strategy. Do we ship minor SDK updates that log warnings, or wait until we can update server and then cut?

maria: Ship minor SDK updates that are opt-in and surface a migration guide. Default to "silent" to avoid user noise but log telemetry if enabled.

tim: Also add a server-side header to encourage auto-migration by SDKs when safe. SDKs can parse and apply small transformations.

leena: Concern: generated adapters might not cover edge cases. We need an escape hatch to route specific client IDs to a dedicated proxy with custom transforms.

sylvia: agreed. add per-client routing to the plan and a "strict" policy for customers who want enforced errors.

raj: timeline estimate looks OK. I'll sketch telemetry event schema and a tiny PoC transform script tomorrow.

maria: I'll draft the deprecation notice copy for customers and put in marketing review.

sylvia: Great. If no objections, I'll update the RFC and open tickets: telemetry, adapter generator, SDK patch, routing rules, deprecation notice.

tim: :thumbsup:

leena: :eyes: please add test plan for adapter regressions (fuzz inputs + golden responses)

sylvia: will do. Thanks all.
